```{r}
library(data.table)
res   <- fread("output/improved_results.csv")
final <- res[.N]
base  <- res[1]
model <- readRDS("shiny_app/final_model.rds")
pct   <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
app_url <- "https://heinhtet.shinyapps.io/shiny_app/"
```

## The problem and the product

- Typing is slow.
- Many words can be guessed from the words you just typed.
- A good suggestion saves.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Next Word Predictor** shows the three most likely next words as you type. One click adds a word.
:::

## How the model works

- Learned from `r format(length(model$vocab), big.mark = ",")` distinct words in blogs, news and Twitter (English).
- Counts which words follow each 1-, 2- and 3-word phrase.
- Looks up the last three words you typed.
- If that phrase was never seen, drops the oldest word and tries again ("backoff").


## How well it works

Tested on text the model never saw:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h2>`r pct(final$top3)`</h2>
right word in the top three

<h2>`r pct(final$top1)`</h2>
right word as first guess
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h2>`r round(final$ms_per_pred)` ms</h2>
per prediction

<h2>`r round(file.size("shiny_app/final_model.rds") / 1024^2, 1)` MB</h2>
model file
:::
::::

The basic model scored `r pct(base$top3)` in the top three on the same test.

## Try the app

**[`r app_url`](`r app_url`)**

1. Type a phrase, e.g. *"thanks for the"*.
2. Three suggested words appear as buttons, best guess first.
3. Click one to add it, and keep typing.
4. The bars show how confident the model is in each word.

Small, fast and simple: ready to build into a keyboard.
